 A guide to Daiso, Korea’s fixed-price chain
 By 
 Hyemin Lee 
 Hyemin Lee 
 Stripes Korea
 • 
 October 28, 2026
 (Photos by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Daiso (다이소) is a Korean fixed-price chain selling everyday items priced from 500 won to 5,000 won. Because the prices are so low, you might assume it’s Korea’s version of a dollar store where you don’t expect much beyond cheap basics. 
 In Korea, though, Daiso has become a place brands compete to get into. More manufacturers now pitch products made just for Daiso. Locals go there not only for daily necessities but also for seasonal items, trendy character goods and snacks. Many families stop by after dinner out or on an evening walk with no plans of buying anything, but simply there to browse. You always find something new, useful or just fun to look at. With about 1,600 stores across the country, you can find a Daiso shop almost anywhere in Korea. If you just arrived in Korea, here’s what to know before your first Daiso trip. 
 *Despite sharing the same name, Daiso in Korea and Japan are operated by separate companies and are not part of the same corporate group. 
 Beauty section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Daiso 101 
 What you can find: If you’re setting up a new home in Korea, Daiso is a great place to start your shopping. You can pick up dishes, kitchen tools, storage containers, toiletries, hand tools and cleaning supplies without spending much. If you’re traveling, you can grab a travel toiletry kit, a charging cable and other small electronics. Or, you can pick up an umbrella when the rain catches you off guard.
 The shelves also change with the season: picnic supplies for spring, beach items for summer, camping accessories for fall and decorations for Halloween and Christmas. Car accessories, pet supplies, toys, party items and materials for school projects or art classes also fill other aisles. 
 Quality : The low prices can make first-time shoppers wonder about quality. Daiso says its quality control team checks products at five points from the factory to the store shelf. To meet its price points, many items also come in smaller packs or simpler sets than regular products. 
 I don’t expect every 1,000-won item to last forever, but plenty of Daiso items in my home have lasted for years. I still use dishes and tools I bought nearly 10 years ago. I’ve found many everyday items there that work just as well as pricier ones I’ve seen elsewhere
 Language and payment: Self-checkout kiosks offer several languages, including English, and international credit cards are accepted.
 Tax refund: Many stores offer tax refunds for eligible travelers. In Korea, the minimum purchase for tax refund is usually 15,000 won. Look for a Tax Refund sign at the store.
 Return and exchanges: You can exchange or return items within two weeks of purchase. Bring the item, the receipt and the card you paid with. Refunds must be processed at the store where you bought the item and the original packaging and tags should be intact.
 Hours : Most stores are open 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. but hours can vary by store.
 Pet section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Halloween section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Toy section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Stores worth checking 
 Good news if you live in Pyeongtaek: two of Korea’s five largest Daiso stores are there according to a store size ranking Daiso released in June 2026. Here are some of popular Daiso stores worth a visit.
 [Seoul] 
 Myeongdong Station branch: 
 One of the most popular Daiso stores among tourists with 12 floors. 
 Naver Map 
 Hongdae 2nd branch: 
 A seven-story store right by Hongik University Station. 
 Naver Map 
 [Pyeongtaek] 
 Pyeongtaek Godeok British branch: 
 Korea’s second largest Daiso, a good one for those near Osan Air Base. Two hours of free parking is available, so ask staff for a parking voucher. 
 Naver Map 
 Pyeongtaek Jungang-ro branch: 
 One of the largest Daiso stores near Pyeongtaek Station. A good option for those at Camp Humphreys. One hour of free parking is available so ask staff for a parking voucher. 
 Naver Map 
 [Daegu] 
 Daegu Dongseong-ro main branch: 
 A large, five-level store in downtown Daegu, good for those near Camp Walker and Camp Henry. 
 Naver Map 
 Gift shopping at Daiso 
 When my friend Lei came to Korea from the Philippines for a BTS concert, she had little time and a long shopping list. She was thoughtful enough to want gifts for literally everyone back home, including her family and co-workers. We had limited time, so I simply took her to Daiso. 
 She found beauty products for her co-workers, character goods for her children and snacks for everyone. What surprised her most was how little everything cost. Her family and co-workers also liked the gifts a lot. 
 Daiso is where I often buy small gifts for my friends overseas. Most items come in small sizes, so I can fit a little of everything into one box and let my friends try a mix of Korean things, from snacks to cute stationery. I usually look for two things: items that are easy to pack and show something about Korea. 
 If you’re shopping for friends and family back home like Lei was, here are the Daiso sections I would recommend.
 Skin care and cosmetics 
 Daiso’s beauty section has become really popular over the past few years, and the shelves now cover skin care, makeup and body care. You’ll find familiar brands such as The Face Shop, AHC, TONYMOLY and Amorepacific’s Mimo. 
 I never thought I’d be someone who buys beauty products at Daiso. My sister, who knows much more about skin care than I, gave me a 3,000 won retinol eye cream from Daiso’s TONYMOLY Boncept line. I loved it. Since then, my trust in Daiso beauty products has grown and I’ve gone back for other skin and body care products. 
 Beauty section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 If you’re interested in Korean skin care but don’t know where to start, head to Daiso. Many products cost just a few thousand won, so it’s worth a look even if Olive Young is on your list. 
 Korean skin care routine usually has four to six steps such as toner, essence, serum, cream and eye cream. Some Daiso lines are set up so you can build the whole routine. Each item costs 3,000–5,000 won, so the full line just comes to around 25,000–30,000 won. After washing your face, apply them from the thinnest texture to the thickest. Sheet facemasks starting at 500 won are another good way to try Korean skin care.
 Beauty section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Korean snacks 
 The snack aisle was where Lei filled most of her basket. Small packs are useful when you want to bring home different flavors without taking up too much space in your suitcase. A few of my favorite snacks are Bichobi chocolate biscuits, Butter Waffle and Malang Cow candies, always good choices when introducing Korean snacks. At Daiso, they come in just the right sizes for sharing. Imported cookies and chips are stacked alongside the Korean brands, so check the package if you specifically want Korean snacks. 
 Snack section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Traditional Korean designs 
 Daiso also has many items inspired by traditional designs, and depending on the store, you can find white moon jars, teacups, fans, bookmarks, stationery and daily items decorated with traditional patterns. Some ceramic pieces are inspired by baekja and cheongja, traditional white porcelain and celadon. The white moon jars are a popular good luck decor item in Korea, so they can be a thoughtful gift for homes. 
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 If you want something special for letters or cards to send home, look for envelopes and paper goods with hanbok or traditional patterns. Decorated money envelopes are common here because Koreans give cash gifts on special occasions like Seollal (Lunar New Year) and birthdays. You can also find gift boxes and cases inspired by minhwa folk painting or mother-of-pearl inlay. 
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Health supplements 
 The supplement section is one of Daiso’s newest. Many Koreans buy health supplements at pharmacies, so shoppers were excited when Daiso launched this section. Most items cost 3,000–5,000 won. The shelves run from basics such as vitamin C and omega-3 to eye health products. Korean red ginseng is also a popular item as it’s a classic gift for parents and elders in Korea. The small packs of Korean health supplements can be a good gift to bring home.  
 Health supplements section (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
 Cute stationery and character goods 
 In Korea, cute characters and playful designs show up everywhere, even on ordinary things. At Daiso, you’ll easily find a variety of cute daily products. The stationery aisle has pens topped with bears, capybaras and sea animals, tiny lunchbox erasers and carrot or puppy pencil cases. The same cute touch shows up on cups, chopsticks, bowls and slippers. Daiso stocks famous international characters like Disney and Doraemon, but for something Korean, look for Kakao Friends. These characters started as emoticons on KakaoTalk, the messaging app most Koreans use every day, and now show up on everything from toys to household goods. If character items aren’t your thing, there are plenty of simpler colors and designs, too. 
 (Photo by Hyemin Lee/Stripes Korea)
